title: The Winter Oath
subtitle: A Rope-Bound Enemies-to-Lovers Romantasy
description:
On the mountain, every lie costs body heat. And every true answer he gives her becomes a line on the queen's map.

Ila is the crown's pass-surveyor, and she believes a map is only ever true or false. Her queen has ordered her to chart every winter way across the closed passes of Hemkot. Without them she will never be Chief Surveyor. To cross, she must be rope-bound to a guide chosen by the hill council.

The guide is Prince Kunal of Neshar. He is charming, sharp-edged and sworn to keep his valley's hidden ways off every map. He spoke against her licence, then tied himself to her wrist so he could choose what she sees. He answers every question with a question. On this rope, he can't lie to her for free, and neither can she.

Kunal is dangerous to her in the way that matters most. Every secret route he shares can be drawn, and every line she draws could bring garrisons to his people's doors. Then Ila opens a sealed letter at the Glass Lakes. It says her family's grave lies beneath the mountain, and the way to it runs through his.

The pass will close forever unless the spirits' Old Bargain is paid. A rebel force is hunting the princes' way. And the man she is falling for may be the heir to the secret that cost her grandfather his life.

Will Ila hand the mountain to the crown, hide it for Neshar, or find the third way, if love can survive the truth?

The Winter Oath is Book 2 of The Winter Passes, a survival-adventure romantasy series. Each book follows a new couple and ends with a happy ever after for that couple. Tropes: enemies to lovers, forced proximity, magical bond, slow burn.

heat_notes: Open door, moderate: two explicit love scenes between consenting adults, each following a truth that changes the bond. Slow burn, with a first kiss at the midpoint.
content_notes: Survival darkness: frostbite and the permanent loss of toes, an avalanche slope, thin-ice peril, hostage threats and a violent confrontation. A beloved supporting character dies (reported, not shown). Grief, a hanging law mentioned as background, and a childhood abandonment remembered. Lies cost the liar body heat through magic. No sexual violence. The love interest's danger points outward and is not used against the heroine. HEA for the couple. A series thread, the Old Bargain, continues into Book 3.
